about: Vectors for the x402 batch-settlement pairings (the x402-batch-settlement entry point of @integraledger/lcp). H is SHA-256("abc") and H' SHA-256("abd"); EVM keys are the published Anvil development accounts 0, 1 and 3; the EVM values were computed with eth-account 0.14.0, eth-abi 6.0.0, eth-utils 6.0.0 and viem 2.57.4 and read them on Base Sepolia; the SVM values with solders 0.26.0, PyNaCl 1.6.2 and @noble/curves 2.4.0. The SVM fixtures (ES4's top_up, request_close and nonce-memo wires, ES5's landed wire, the no-channel transaction) were built with solders 0.26.0 on Python 3.11; the same script reproduces ES1, ES2, ES3 and ES5's txid. The receiver authorizer is the key of seed 03x32. An SVM opening carries two Memo instructions, the seller memo (extra.memo, L) and then x402's receiver-authorizer binding memo, whose UTF-8 data is x402:batch-settlement:svm:rcvauth:v1: and the base58 key (x402-foundation/x402 751590a2, specs/schemes/batch-settlement/scheme_batch_settlement_svm.md L121-127 and L1320-1325; the order is the steward SDK's, typescript/packages/mechanisms/svm/src/payment-channels/open.ts:464-467, and the text its batch-settlement/receiverBinding.ts:19 and test/unit/batch.receiverAuthorizer.test.ts, "round-trips the binding memo and rejects anything else", at the same commit).

ES6.case: a full refund: buildWithin with refund {} carries the voucher for maxClaimableAmount, the server's accepted cumulative amount, with expiresAt 0, and no amount; with recentBlockhash it also carries a payer-signed request_close, which x402 sends only on a retry after invalid_batch_settlement_svm_receiver_binding_unavailable (x402-foundation/x402 751590a2, scheme_batch_settlement_svm.md L626-636; the steward SDK's typescript/packages/mechanisms/svm/src/batch-settlement/client/channel.ts:281-312, and test/unit/batch.refund.test.ts, "resends with a request_close when the facilitator has no binding", at the same commit). The request_close is the Compute Budget prefix (limit 200000, price 1 microlamport), request_close (data 05) of the payment-channels program with exactly the payer (read-only signer) and the channel PDA (writable), then one Memo v3 with extra.memo when the option carries one, else none; fee payer extra.feePayer.

cooperative.case: ES4's option and config, maxClaimableAmount 1000, no recentBlockhash: one ed25519-raw request by the payer authorizer over ES3's message; the payload is {type: refund, channelConfig, voucher}

withMemo.case: the retry, with ES4's option (extra.memo = L) and recentBlockhash: the solana-message request, then the voucher; decompiled, the message has the fee payer, blockhash and instructions of the one inside ES4.closeWireBase64, built with solders 0.26.0 (key order inside a category is not compared: the rail does not fix it); the payload is {type: refund, channelConfig, voucher, transaction}

withoutMemo.case: the retry, with ES4's option without extra.memo

loneSurrogateMemo.case: the retry, with ES4's option whose extra.memo holds a lone surrogate (U+D800): a string with no UTF-8 form (The Unicode Standard 16.0, section 3.9, D92: UTF-8 encodes no surrogate code point; Python 3's str.encode('utf-8') raises UnicodeEncodeError for it), so the request_close's memo cannot carry the bytes the caller gave, and nothing is built

ES7.case: svmLocate for the opening, with no transaction named: the fee payer's signatures list ES5's txid, whose RPC memo rendering is '[77] ' + L + '; [81] ' + the binding memo (getSignaturesForAddress renders each memo as '[len] text' and joins them with '; ': anza-xyz/agave transaction-status/src/extract_memos.rs at 3deb741d), then one signature below fromSlot. Each candidate is read through the pairing's own status (svmChannelStatus): the opening is found. Read through the transfer test instead, the opening, which carries no top-level transfer, is not found and the search would end complete and empty.

ES8.case: the opening's memos: exactly one receiver-authorizer binding memo and exactly one other Memo instruction, in either order, the other carrying H; any other count is refused (x402-foundation/x402 751590a2, scheme_batch_settlement_svm.md L1320-1325 and L1346-1348: the open suffix carries exactly one binding Memo and the facilitator requires exactly one Memo besides it; the steward SDK's payment-channels/open.ts:1199-1224 and test/unit/batch.receiverAuthorizer.test.ts, "requires exactly one matching binding memo in the open", which rejects an open with no binding memo and one with two). Each wire is ES2's opening with only its memos changed, built with solders 0.26.0 and signed by the payer; bound reads it as deposit.transaction under ES4's option and config, and recover reads it landed.

ES9.case: pairingOf and advertise of fixed.svm.option, whose extra.withdrawDelay is 3600, with maxTimeoutSeconds replaced by each row's value. x402 751590a2, scheme_batch_settlement_svm.md L235 and L247: maxTimeoutSeconds is a number, and withdrawDelay MUST be >= maxTimeoutSeconds. That comparison is read only when maxTimeoutSeconds is a JSON number, never by converting a string or an array to one; an option whose maxTimeoutSeconds is of another type is named, and advertise refuses it, as build does, because its timeout is not a positive safe integer. A row without maxTimeoutSeconds removes the member. expectAdvertise null: the option is advertised.

ES10.case: The point rule a PDA candidate meets: 32 bytes are a point when ed25519.Point.fromBytes(bytes, true) of @noble/curves 2.4.0 accepts them, decompression only: y is the little-endian integer with bit 255 cleared, taken modulo p = 2^255 - 19, and x^2 = (y^2 - 1) / (d y^2 + 1) must have a square root, so x = 0 with the sign bit set decodes. Each row's point value is Python 3's integer arithmetic (Euler's criterion), and noble agrees.

agreedRefusals.about: Refusal codes the batch-settlement specification leaves to the implementation. A row with pairing and call runs that pairing's function: with choice, call(choice, H); with h, build of ES2's choice, the advertised Solana option with the svm payer as payer and payerAuthorizer, deposit, salt 42, openSlot, tokenProgram and blockhash as recentBlockhash, with that h; with zeroMembers, the EVM build of EB2 and EB3's opening once per member named, with that member the zero address: from in its choice, or payTo or asset in fixed.evm.option. A row with pairing and calls runs each of those functions of that pairing on an opening. On the EVM pairing it is EB2 and EB3's opening: the EVM build of fixed.evm.option advertised under H, with the payer, payer authorizer, deposit, authSalt and now of fixed.evm, completed with EB3's and EB2's signatures, and the same build for a Permit2 deposit (the option's extra.assetTransferMethod permit2), completed with the same signatures, which no read verifies; buildWithin takes the advertised option and EB2's maxClaimableAmount. On the Solana pairing it is ES2's opening as ES4 presents it: ES4's config, a voucher for ES1's PDA, and ES2's wire as deposit.transaction; buildWithin takes the advertised Solana option and maxClaimableAmount 1000. With depositAmount, deposit.amount is replaced by it. With validBeforeOrDeadline, the ERC-3009 authorization's validBefore, or the Permit2 authorization's deadline, is replaced by it. With configMembers, each member set replaces those members of channelConfig, one run per set; voucher.channelId is the channel id of the configuration that results, and buildWithin takes that configuration, under H. With refundAmounts, each value is the amount of a refund payload that carries the opening's channelConfig and voucher, one run per value.

buyer.about: The buyer gate's rows for this file's pairings, in the form of buyer.json's rows. B2 is the plant: the document advertises H, the hash of the ATR in B6's first check, and the link serves the planted ATR, that ATR with one byte changed; the gate declines hash-mismatch and never calls the signer. B6 is the pairing's bound check over the payment this file already holds: check(ATR, presented) gives H, and check(planted ATR, presented) declines signed-not-bound. Where the ATR is abc, H is its SHA-256 (FIPS 180-2 B.1) and the planted ATR is abd. SHA-256 values are GNU coreutils sha256sum, which openssl dgst -sha256 matches. Bytes are hex. A B2 input names the account, the buyer's inputs and the time (now, in seconds) its build needs. noSignedPayment names each pairing of the file that has no B6 row, and why.
